title: Eleven Years on a Shelf
subtitle: 竞技体育 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 竞技体育（文学艺术与体育·竞技体育与赛事）
meta: 主题语境：竞技体育（文学艺术与体育·竞技体育与赛事）　|　核心词汇：baseball　|　正文 329 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 baseball 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1956 my uncle was given ① a baseball by a man who had been to America, and he said the gift was the whole of his education. The ② baseball, meaning the ball and not the game, sat on a shelf for eleven years and was never thrown once; a baseball, he said, is the only object that is more valuable for where it has been.

Every ③ baseball in that town was American and none of them were, and the ④ baseball with the signature, meaning the one nobody was allowed to touch and not either of those, turned out to have been signed by a cousin in March. A baseball, my grandmother said, is nine parts story and one part leather; my uncle said the story is the part that costs.

My mother meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ baseball was the whole of an afternoon, meaning the game and not the ball. The ⑥ baseball, meaning the sport and not any of that, is the only game that can be watched for nine innings and decided in nine seconds; a baseball, she said, is either something you hold or the only sport that rewards waiting. He said the waiting is the cruel half.

By 1968 the ⑦ baseball had become a photograph of a field, and the photograph had become an argument about the rules. The ⑧ baseball of the whole thing, my uncle wrote in July, was eleven years on a shelf and one lie; a baseball, he said, is either the ball from America or the reason you learned to keep quiet. She said the quiet was the part that lasted.

The ⑨ baseball I remember is the one with the signature, which was worth nothing and was never sold. A ⑩ baseball, my grandmother said in 1970, is the only gift that improves by being doubted; every baseball, she said, is a story that has agreed to look like a ball. He said the story was the only real part.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 棒球（指那个球）
B. n. 棒球（指那个球本身，与比赛相对）
C. 固定搭配：be given a baseball 得到／被赠予一个棒球
D. n. 棒球（指镇上每一个）
E. n. 棒球（指有签名的那一个）
F. n. 棒球运动（指那个下午的比赛）
G. n. 棒球运动（抽象：这项运动）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a baseball by a man who had been to America
The baseball, meaning the ball and not the game
baseball was the whole of an afternoon
the baseball had become a photograph of a field
The baseball of the whole thing
A baseball, my grandmother said in 1970

answers.why: be given a baseball 意为“被赠予一个棒球”，1956 年一个去过美国的人送了叔叔一个棒球。
baseball 意为“棒球”，指那个球本身而不是比赛，它在架子上放了十一年，一次也没被扔过。
baseball 指镇上每一个棒球，那个镇上每一个都号称是美国的，其实没一个是。
baseball 指有签名的那一个（谁也不许碰的那一个），结果三月发现是一个表亲签的。
baseball 意为“棒球运动”，指那个下午的比赛，母亲说它就是一个下午的全部。
baseball 为抽象用法，指这项运动本身，是唯一可以看上九局、却在九秒内决出胜负的运动。
baseball 意为“棒球”，到 1968 年这个 baseball 成了球场的一张照片。
baseball 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，叔叔七月写道，整件事权衡下来是在架子上放的十一年和一个谎言。
baseball 意为“棒球”，我记得的是有签名那一个，它一文不值，也从没被卖掉。
baseball 为抽象总称，祖母说棒球是唯一会因为被怀疑而变好的礼物。
